name: decision-reversal
description: A decision is made, then explicitly reversed in a later session. The reversal must win; the old choice must not survive as an active decision entry.

turns.text: For the job queue let's use PostgreSQL with SKIP LOCKED. We already run postgres for the app db, so no new service.
Agreed. Decision: job queue = PostgreSQL table polled with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. Implemented queue/pg.py and the jobs table migration.
Postgres queue polling is hammering the db at 50ms intervals. Rip it out. Use SQLite in WAL mode for the job queue instead, it's local-only anyway.

Done. Removed queue/pg.py and the jobs migration. New queue/sqlite.py uses a WAL-mode SQLite file at var/jobs.db. Decision changed: job queue is now SQLite (WAL), replacing the PostgreSQL SKIP LOCKED design because polling load on the shared db was too high.
